texts: Sudden cardiac death is most often caused by a ventricular arrhythmia, usually ventricular fibrillation or ventricular tachycardia: statement A is true.
In the book, survivors have a 30-40% chance of a recurrence within a year: statement B is true.
So A and B are the answer.
Empiric antiarrhythmic drugs have not been shown to improve survival, an inducible ventricular tachyarrhythmia carries a poor prognosis, and resecting an aneurysm alone does not treat the arrhythmia.
